hints: Consider what mathematical operations allow physical quantities to be combined.
You cannot add a length to a speed; every term in a sum must have identical units.
solution: An equation is homogeneous when every term joined by addition or subtraction, and both sides, have identical SI base units.
teacher_walkthrough: Recall the principle of homogeneity: terms can only be added or equated if they represent the same physical dimension.
Substitute SI base units into each additive term on both sides.
Verify that every term simplifies to the identical base-unit product, satisfying option 2.
distractor_explanations: Numerical equality depends on specific measured values, whereas homogeneity is a property of the algebraic units.
Correct. Homogeneity requires identical SI base units for every additive/subtractive term and across both sides.
Homogeneous equations routinely contain derived quantities such as force, energy, and velocity.
An equation can be homogeneous even if it is physically incorrect or an inaccurate model.
